{{short description|Family of graphs whose shallow minors are sparse graphs}}

In [[graph theory]], a family of [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graphs]] is said to have '''bounded expansion''' if all of its [[shallow minor]]s are [[sparse graph]]s. Many natural families of sparse graphs have bounded expansion. A closely related but stronger property,  '''polynomial expansion''', is equivalent to the existence of [[planar separator theorem|separator theorem]]s for these families. Families with these properties have efficient [[algorithm]]s for problems including the [[subgraph isomorphism problem]] and [[model checking]] for the first order theory of graphs.

==Definition and equivalent characterizations==
A ''t''-shallow minor of a graph ''G'' is defined to be a graph formed from ''G'' by contracting a collection of vertex-disjoint subgraphs of radius ''t'', and deleting the remaining vertices of ''G''. A family of graphs has bounded expansion if there exists a function ''f'' such that, in every ''t''-shallow minor of a graph in the family, the ratio of edges to vertices is at most ''f''(''t'').<ref name="no">{{citation
 | last1 = Nešetřil | first1 = Jaroslav | author1-link = Jaroslav Nešetřil
 | last2 = Ossona de Mendez | first2 = Patrice | author2-link = Patrice Ossona de Mendez
 | contribution = 5.5 Classes with Bounded Expansion
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-27875-4
 | isbn = 978-3-642-27874-7
 | mr = 2920058
 | pages = 104–107
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Algorithms and Combinatorics
 | title = Sparsity: Graphs, Structures, and Algorithms
 | volume = 28
 | year = 2012}}.</ref>

Equivalent definitions of classes of bounded expansions are that all shallow minors have [[chromatic number]] bounded by a function of ''t'',<ref name="no"/> or that the given family has a bounded value of a ''topological parameter''. Such a parameter is a [[graph invariant]] that is monotone under taking subgraphs, such that the parameter value can change only in a controlled way when a graph is subdivided, and such that a bounded parameter value implies that a graph has bounded [[degeneracy (graph theory)|degeneracy]].<ref name="now">{{citation
 | last1 = Nešetřil | first1 = Jaroslav | author1-link = Jaroslav Nešetřil
 | last2 = Ossona de Mendez | first2 = Patrice | author2-link = Patrice Ossona de Mendez
 | last3 = Wood | first3 = David R. | author3-link = David Wood (mathematician)
 | arxiv = 0902.3265
 | doi = 10.1016/j.ejc.2011.09.008
 | issue = 3
 | journal = [[European Journal of Combinatorics]]
 | mr = 2864421
 | pages = 350–373
 | title = Characterisations and examples of graph classes with bounded expansion
 | volume = 33
 | year = 2012| s2cid = 2633083 }}.</ref>

==Polynomial expansion and separator theorems==
A stronger notion is '''polynomial expansion''', meaning that the function ''f'' used to bound the edge density of shallow minors is a [[polynomial]]. If a hereditary graph family obeys a [[Planar separator theorem|separator theorem]], stating that any ''n''-vertex graph in the family can be split into pieces with at most ''n''/2 vertices by the removal of ''O''(''n''<sup>''c''</sup>) vertices for some constant ''c''&nbsp;<&nbsp;1, then that family necessarily has polynomial expansion. Conversely, graphs with polynomial expansion have sublinear separator theorems.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Dvořák | first1 = Zdeněk
 | last2 = Norin | first2 = Sergey
 | arxiv = 1504.04821
 | doi = 10.1137/15M1017569
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]
 | mr = 3504982
 | pages = 1095–1101
 | title = Strongly sublinear separators and polynomial expansion
 | volume = 30
 | year = 2016| s2cid = 27395359
 }}</ref>

==Classes of graphs with bounded expansion==
Because of the connection between separators and expansion, every [[Robertson–Seymour theorem|minor-closed graph family]], including the family of [[planar graph]]s, has polynomial expansion. The same is true for [[1-planar graph]]s, and more generally the graphs that can be embedded onto surfaces of bounded [[genus (mathematics)|genus]] with a bounded number of crossings per edge, as well as the [[biclique-free graph|biclique-free]] [[string graph]]s, since these all obey similar separator theorems to the planar graphs.<ref>{{harvtxt|Nešetřil|Ossona de Mendez|2012}}, 14.2 Crossing Number, pp.&nbsp;319–321.</ref><ref>{{citation

Although graphs of bounded [[book thickness]] do not have sublinear separators,<ref>{{citation|title=3-Monotone Expanders|first1=Vida|last1=Dujmović|first2=Anastasios|last2=Sidiropoulos|first3=David R.|last3=Wood|author3-link = David Wood (mathematician)|arxiv=1501.05020|year=2015|bibcode=2015arXiv150105020D}}</ref> they also have bounded expansion.<ref>{{harvtxt|Nešetřil|Ossona de Mendez|2012}}, 14.5 Stack Number, pp. 327–328.</ref> Other graphs of bounded expansion include graphs of bounded degree,<ref>{{harvtxt|Nešetřil|Ossona de Mendez|2012}}, p.&nbsp;307.</ref> [[random graph]]s of bounded average degree in the [[Erdős–Rényi model]],<ref>{{harvtxt|Nešetřil|Ossona de Mendez|2012}}, 14.1 Random Graphs (Erdős–Rényi Model), pp.&nbsp;314–319.</ref> and graphs of bounded [[queue number]].<ref name="now"/><ref>{{harvtxt|Nešetřil|Ossona de Mendez|2012}}, pp.&nbsp;321–327.</ref>

==Algorithmic applications==
Instances of the [[subgraph isomorphism problem]] in which the goal is to find a target graph of bounded size, as a subgraph of a larger graph whose size is not bounded, may be solved in [[linear time]] when the larger graph belongs to a family of graphs of bounded expansion. The same is true for [[clique problem|finding cliques]] of a fixed size, finding [[dominating set]]s of a fixed size, or more generally testing properties that can be expressed by a formula of bounded size in the first-order [[logic of graphs]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Nešetřil|Ossona de Mendez|2012}}, 18.3 The Subgraph Isomorphism Problem and Boolean Queries, pp.&nbsp;400–401.</ref><ref>{{citation

 | contribution = Deciding first-order properties for sparse graphs
